heading: REGIONAL GAZETTE
translated_text:
REGIONAL GAZETTE

PADANGSIDIMPUAN CITY

PEMKO-PSP. Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Padang Sidempuan City.

heading: MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN
MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN
translated_text:
MAYOR OF PADANG SIDEMPUAN

HAS DECIDED:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

heading: CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Padang Sidempuan.
2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
3. Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
4. Mayor is the Mayor of Padang Sidempuan.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD of Padang Sidempuan City is the Regional People's Representative Institution which is positioned as an element of Regional Government Administration.
6. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Women Empowerment and Child Protection System is the entire process of organizing women empowerment and child protection carried out comprehensively, inclusively, and integratively starting from the stage of report/complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal assistance, up to repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of crime and violence to their social environment.
9. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.

2021, No.3 -76­

10. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
11. Victim is a person who experiences physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by a criminal act.
12. Violence is any act that causes injury or death to another person or causes physical damage or property of another person.
13. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
14. Violence against children is any action that results in or may result in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
15. Victim is a woman and child who experiences violence and/or suffering as a result of violence and/or threat of violence.
16. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
18. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional area to the area of origin.
20. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

21. Prevention is a direct effort made by the regional government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.

22. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and self-recovery of victims of violence.
23. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
24. Child-Friendly City hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business world commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

2021, No. 3 -77­

25. Child-friendly city task force hereinafter abbreviated as KLA task force is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA.
29. Business Entity is an institution that carries out daily activities seeking profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children.
26. Sadan Usaha is an institution that carries out daily activities seeking profit and gain, but has a commitment to the protection of women and children.
27. Social welfare is a condition of fulfillment of material, spiritual, and social needs of citizens so that they can live properly and are able to develop themselves, so that they can carry out their social functions.
28. Gender mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of national development program policies.
29. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the regional government or community-based, which includes: referral center, business consultation center, reproductive health consultation center, legal consultation center, integrated crisis center (PKT), integrated service center (PPT), trauma recovery center (trauma center), women's crisis handling center (women crisis center), training center, science and technology information center (PIPTEK), safe house (shelter), transit house, children's friend telephone (TESA) 129, or other forms.

heading: CHAPTER II
CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES

Article 3

1. The purpose of the establishment of this Regional Regulation is to provide a foundation of legal certainty in Women Empowerment and Child Protection activities in the Region.

2021, No. 3 -78­

(2) The implementation of Women and Child Protection aims to:
a. improve the quality of life of women, children, and family quality;
b. increase the institutional capacity of women empowerment and child protection including the development of gender and child data systems;
c. provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including special protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment;
d. provide guidance to the regional government, in planning protection strategies and policies for women and children; and
e. prevent violations of the rights of women and children.

heading: CHAPTER IV
CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS

Part One

Rights of Women and Children

heading: Article 5
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Obligations of Regional Government

heading: Article 6
Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Obligations of the Community

heading: Article 7
translated_text:
Article 7

1. The obligations of the community in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the authorities; and
c. supervise the law enforcement process against cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
2. The obligations of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) are based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.
3. The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards child protection are implemented through community role activities in the implementation of child protection.
4. The obligations and responsibilities of the community towards child protection are implemented through community role activities in the implementation of child protection.
5. The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in paragraph (4) are implemented by involving community organizations, academics, and child observers.

2021, No. 3 -81­

heading: Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Obligations of the Family

heading: Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

The family in efforts to protect the rights of women is obliged to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities for women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent violations of women's rights in the household.

heading: Article 9
CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

FORMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 10

Forms of violence include:
a. physical violence;
b. psychological violence;
c. sexual violence; and/or
d. domestic neglect.

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

Physical violence as referred to in Article 10 letter a results in:
a. the victim becomes ill or seriously injured;
b. death of the victim; and
c. causes disease or impediment to carrying out work, position or livelihood or daily activities.

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

Psychological violence as referred to in Article 10 letter b results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

2021, No. 3 -82­

heading: Article 13
translated_text:
Article 13

Sexual violence as referred to in Article 10 letter c is in the form of:
a. acts of sexual harassment;
b. coercion of sexual relations in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
c. coercion of sexual relations with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

heading: Article 14
CHAPTER VII
Article 16
SERVICES FOR VICTIMS OF ACTS OF VIOLENCE
Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

1. Health Services are provided by health workers at health facilities owned by the government, regional government, and the community, including the private sector, by providing treatment services and health recovery for victims.
2. Victim assistance is provided by health workers, social workers, volunteer assistants, and/or spiritual counselors by providing counseling, spiritual guidance and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims.
3. Provision of counseling is carried out by social workers, volunteer assistants, by listening empathetically and exploring problems for the psychological strengthening of victims.
4. Spiritual guidance is provided by spiritual counselors by providing explanations regarding their rights and obligations, as well as strengthening faith and piety in accordance with the religion and beliefs they adhere to.
5. Victim resocialization is carried out by social agencies and social institutions so that victims can resume their social functions in society.

heading: CHAPTER IX
CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

INFORMATION SYSTEM FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN DATA

Article 20

1. Information system is a system for collecting, preparing, storing, processing, analyzing and/or disseminating information.
2. Gender and Child Data System is the institutionalization of gender and child data management consisting of components-components-components of regulations, institutions, and mechanisms in ministries/agencies and regions in the context of planning, implementation, evaluation, and reporting of the results of policies/programs/activities of development that is gender responsive and child-friendly.
3. Gender Data is data regarding the relationship of relations in status, roles and conditions between men and women.
(4) Disaggregated Data is data disaggregated by sex, age, status and condition of women across all development sectors including health, education, economy and employment, politics and decision-making, law and socio-culture and violence.

5. Types of gender and child data:
a. gender data:
1. gender data in the economic sector including gender issues in labor, cooperatives, SMEs, industry and trade, agriculture, forestry, fisheries and marine affairs, transportation, science and technology and infrastructure;
2. gender data in the political, social and legal sectors;
3. data on the protection of women's rights; and
4. data on family welfare and resilience development.
b. child data:
1. civil rights and freedoms;
2. family environment and alternative care;
3. basic health and welfare;
4. education, leisure time utilization and cultural activities; and
5. special protection.
6. Gender analysis is the process of analyzing disaggregated data by sex conducted systematically with the intention of identifying gender issues and factors that can influence development, particularly related to gender equality issues that are the goals of development.

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

1. The Guidelines for the Implementation of the Gender and Child Data System are intended as a reference for ministries/agencies and regions in providing and utilizing disaggregated data for planning, formulating, implementing, monitoring, evaluating and reporting gender-responsive and child-friendly development policies/programs/activities.
2. Improving the availability and utilization of gender and child data and information in the formulation, planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of development programs/activities.

heading: Article 22
Article 23
translated_text:
Article 23

1. Gender Mainstreaming or abbreviated as PUG is a strategy carried out rationally and systematically to achieve and realize gender equality and gender justice in a number of aspects of human life (household, community and State), through policies and programs that take into account the experiences and aspirations, needs and problems of women and men in the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all policies in various aspects of life and development.
2. In an effort to accelerate gender mainstreaming institutionalization in all SKPD, a PUG Working Group is formed.
3. Members of the PUG Working Group are all heads/leaders of SKPD.
4. The Mayor appoints the head of Bapeda as chairman of the PUG Working Group and the head of the SKPD in charge of women's empowerment as Secretary of the PUG Working Group.
5. The establishment of the PUG Working Group is stipulated by Mayor's Decree.

heading: Article 24
Article 25
Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. Regional Apparatus/Agencies submit reports on the women and children data information system to the Mayor through the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection of Padang Sidempuan City.
2. Reporting of implementation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out annually and/or at any time if necessary.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

1. Every person, community institution, university and business entity has the right to utilize the women and children data information system of Padang Sidempuan City by citing the data.
2. Every person, community institution, university and business entity may partner as a provider or user of gender and child data and information to the organizer of the women and children data information system of Padang Sidempuan City for subsequent verification, inputting and publication.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

CHILDREN'S FORUM

Article 28

1. The Regional Government is obliged to establish a children's forum at the Padang Sidempuan City level as participation through the children's forum.
2. The children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) represents children, both representing children's geographical domicile, components of children's socio-cultural groups and children's educational backgrounds as well as accommodating the interests of children with special needs.
3. In every formulation of policies related to children, the Regional Government must consider and accommodate the opinions of children conveyed through the children's forum.
4. The establishment of the children's forum as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by Mayor's Decree.
5. Sources of funding for the implementation of children's forum activities may come from:

a. contributions from members of the children's forum;

2021, No. 3 -88­

b. donations from the community/private parties that are legal and non-binding in nature;
c. assistance from the City Government; and/ or
d. other sources of funding in accordance with laws and regulations.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

1. Establishment of the Padang Sidempuan City Children's Forum, participants in the meeting to establish the district/city children's forum are delegates or representatives of the sub-district children's forum of at least one boy and one girl, the number of representatives is adjusted to the needs and number of sub-districts in the Padang Sidempuan City area
2. Establishment of the Sub-district Children's Forum, participants in the meeting to establish the Sub-district Children's Forum are delegates or representatives of the village/sub-district children's forum of at least one boy and one girl. The number of representatives is adjusted to the needs and number of villages/sub-districts in the sub-district area
3. Establishment of the Village/Sub-district Children's Forum, children are invited to represent their respective activity groups, at least one boy and one girl from each children's activity group, subsequently the child representatives from the activity groups become the main participants in the establishment of the Village/Sub-district Children's Forum.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 30

In the context of implementing the Protection of Women and Children, the following are established:

a. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children (P2TP2A);
b. Family Welfare Consultation Institution; and
c. Other institutions in accordance with needs and/or provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: Article 31
Article 32
Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

1. The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) is under the coordination of regional apparatus work units (SKPD) or other units handling women's empowerment and child protection.
2. The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as referred to in paragraph (1) does not have authority in the formulation of policies related to women's empowerment and child protection.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment and Protection (P2TP2A) functions as:

a. an information center for women and children;

2021, No. 3 -90­
b. a service center for women and victims of violence; and
c. an empowerment center for women and children.

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

1. The Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment and Protection (P2TP2A) at City Level shall be established based on a Mayor Decree and a Sub-district Head Decree for the sub-district level.
2. Membership of the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment and Protection (P2TP2A) may come from elements of regional apparatus, professional organizations, academics, community leaders and other elements as needed.
3. Further provisions regarding P2TP2A shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

The Family Learning Center (PUSPAGA) is a form of preventive service under the coordination of the Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as a manifestation of state concern in improving family life and family resilience through education or parenting programs, parenting skills, child protection skills, ability to increase child participation in the family as well as counseling program services for children and families.

heading: CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

CHILD-FRIENDLY CITY

Part One

Principles and Objectives

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

To ensure the fulfillment of children's rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination, real integrated efforts are needed between the Regional Government, community and business sector through the development of a Child-Friendly City.

heading: Article 38
Article 39
Article 40
Article 41
translated_text:
Article 41

1. To make the development of a Child-Friendly City effective, a Child-Friendly City Task Force shall be established as determined by Mayor Decree.
2. Membership of the Child-Friendly City Task Force may come from the Regional Government, child representatives, business sector, religious leaders, community leaders and other parties as needed.

heading: Article 42
CHAPTER XIV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIV

FUNDING

Article 43

1. The Regional Government is obligated to provide budget for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection programs and activities.
2. Financing for the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection activities as referred to in paragraph (1) is sourced from:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget (APBD); and
b. other lawful and non-binding sources based on the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XV
translated_text:
CHAPTER XV

COMMUNITY PARTICIPATION

Article 44

1. The community may participate in the implementation of women's empowerment activities.
2. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by individuals, community groups and community organizations.
3. Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. cooperation;
b. active role in policy formulation; and
c. complaints/reports.
4. The procedures for community participation as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER XVI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XVI

COOPERATION

Article 45

1. Regional cooperation is a joint effort between regions with other regions, between regions and third parties, and/or between regions and institutions or regional governments abroad based on a balance of efficiency and effectiveness of public services and mutual benefit.
2. Regional cooperation with third parties, hereinafter abbreviated as KSDPK, is a joint effort carried out by regions with third parties in the context of administering governmental affairs that are regional authorities to improve community welfare and accelerate the fulfillment of public services.
3. In order to achieve the objectives of protecting the rights of women and children from acts of violence, the regional government cooperates with:
a. other provinces;
b. regencies/cities; and
c. non-governmental institutions
4. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (3) includes:
a. exchange of data and information;
b. rehabilitation of victims of violence;
c. repatriation and social reintegration; and
d. provision of evidence and witnesses which are followed up in accordance with applicable law.

heading: Article 46
CHAPTER XVII
CHAPTER XVIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XVIII

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 48

Any person who commits a criminal act/violence as referred to in Article 11, Article 12, Article 13, and Article 14 shall be threatened with criminal punishment in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: CHAPTER XIX
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIX

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 49

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, orders the promulgation of this Regional Regulation by placing it in the Regional Gazette of Padang Sidempuan City.

Enacted in Padang Sidempuan on 16 March 2021
